title: Architecture analysis: Agent anchor mechanism for post-compaction state recovery
summary: Implement a persistent per-agent state anchoring system that enables coherent recovery after context window clears. Agents write compact JSON anchor files (2KB soft / 3KB hard limit) to `.egg-state/agent-anchors/<agent-id>.json` via `egg-orch anchor` CLI commands. Cross-agent reads go through orchestrator API endpoints (following the contract_api.py cross-worktree pattern). The orchestrator generates a team-level anchor projection. Context compaction is replaced with full context clear + anchor reload via standing rules in `sandbox/.claude/rules/anchor-recovery.md`. The implementation spans 4 layers: (1) shared Python library + JSON schema, (2) orchestrator API + Redis persistence + CLI subcommands, (3) gateway phase filter + container spawner integration, (4) agent recovery rules + checkpoint capture.

problem_statement.description: Long-running agents in BRC concurrent phases lose working state when the context window fills. Without a structured recovery mechanism, agents repeat work, forget inter-agent decisions, break consensus, and re-attempt failed approaches. The existing recovery mechanisms (consensus_wrapper.py restart prompts, egg-contract pipeline-level tasks, post-session checkpoints, Redis message bus) are either too coarse, too late, or lack the agent-scoped granularity needed for mid-session recovery.

root_causes.title: No agent-scoped persistent working state
root_causes.description: egg-contract tracks pipeline-level tasks and decisions, not per-agent working state like 'I'm on sub-task 3 of 7' or 'coder and I agreed on approach B'. The granularity gap means agents cannot reconstruct their working context after a context clear.

root_causes.title: Consensus wrapper only handles clean exits, not mid-session compaction
root_causes.description: consensus_wrapper.py's _RECOVERY_SYSTEM_PROMPT handles restart scenarios where the agent exits entirely. It cannot recover from mid-session context clears because the agent process is still running — only its in-memory context is lost.

root_causes.title: Checkpoints are post-session, not live state
root_causes.description: Checkpoint captures happen at session-end triggers via checkpoint_handler.py. They cannot be read during the same session for recovery — they're audit artifacts, not live recovery points.

root_causes.title: Message bus lacks state summarization
root_causes.description: Redis message bus (redis_message_store.py) persists all messages via Redis Streams, but after context clear an agent doesn't know which messages are relevant or what decisions they represent. Raw message replay is insufficient without an anchor that provides the 'last known good state' reference point.

current_architecture.execution_model: BRC (Broadcast-Review-Converge) peer consensus with concurrent execution. PeerConsensusTracker in peer_consensus.py manages per-agent state machines (WORKING → PROPOSED → CONFIRMED for producers, WORKING → REVIEWING → CONFIRMED for reviewers). ConcurrentExecutor spawns containers with shared worktrees. Agents communicate via orchestrator message bus and coordinate via consensus commands.
current_architecture.recovery_model: Two-level: (1) consensus_wrapper.py wraps agent command with bash trap for SIGTERM and restart-on-exit logic, injecting _RECOVERY_SYSTEM_PROMPT with BRC state on restart (max 2 restarts). (2) egg-contract provides pipeline-level task tracking readable via egg-contract show. Neither handles mid-session context loss.
current_architecture.storage_model: Pipeline state in Redis (orchestrator state_store.py), messages in Redis Streams (redis_message_store.py), progress events in-memory (progress_store.py), contracts as JSON files in .egg-state/contracts/, agent outputs as JSON in .egg-state/agent-outputs/. Phase permissions enforce file access via gateway/phase_filter.py.

key_components.name: PeerConsensusTracker
key_components.description: Manages BRC state machines per agent. Tracks proposal versions, ACKs, NACKs, review assignments. The anchor's brc_state section must mirror this tracker's state for recovery.

key_components.name: ConsensusWrapper
key_components.description: Builds shell wrapper that restarts agents on premature exit. Injects _RECOVERY_SYSTEM_PROMPT with BRC state. Must be extended to load anchor in recovery prompt.

key_components.name: ContainerSpawner
key_components.description: Creates Docker containers with gateway sessions, env vars (EGG_AGENT_ROLE, EGG_PIPELINE_ID, etc.), mounts, and network config. Must add AGENT_ANCHOR_ID env var and compaction-disabled flag.

key_components.name: PhaseFilter
key_components.description: Enforces phase-specific file restrictions on git push. Uses PhaseFileRestriction with allowed_patterns and blocked_patterns. Must add .egg-state/agent-anchors/* to allowed patterns for all phases.

key_components.name: ProgressStore
key_components.description: Thread-safe in-memory store for per-pipeline progress events. Anchor store will follow this same pattern with Redis persistence added.

key_components.name: ContractLoader
key_components.description: Atomic read/write for JSON contract files using tempfile+rename pattern. The egg_anchor library must use the same atomic write approach.

key_components.name: Orchestrator API
key_components.description: Flask app with Blueprint-based route modules (progress.py, messages.py, signals.py, etc.). New anchors.py Blueprint needed following the same pattern.

key_components.name: Agent Rules
key_components.description: Standing instruction files loaded at container startup. Contains mission.md, contract.md, orchestrator.md, etc. New anchor-recovery.md needed.

recommended_approach.title: Layered implementation with shared library core
recommended_approach.summary: Implement in 4 implementation tasks mapped to the 4 layers: (1) Schema + shared library (egg_anchor), (2) Orchestrator API + Redis store + CLI, (3) Gateway phase filter + container spawner, (4) Agent rules + consensus wrapper + checkpoint integration. Each layer builds on the previous. The shared library provides models and atomic I/O. The orchestrator serves as the cross-agent anchor broker. The gateway enforces ownership. Agent rules enable pull-based recovery.
recommended_approach.justification: This layered approach minimizes cross-cutting changes per task, enables independent testing of each layer, and follows established codebase patterns (egg_contracts for shared lib, progress_store for orchestrator store, phase_filter for gateway enforcement). The single-writer design eliminates concurrency complexity. API-mediated cross-agent reads follow the proven contract_api.py pattern.

architecture_decisions.title: Shared library at shared/egg_anchor/ (not orchestrator-internal)
architecture_decisions.decision: Place the anchor models, loader, and validator in a new shared/egg_anchor/ package
architecture_decisions.rationale: Both the orchestrator (for API endpoints and team anchor generation) and the sandbox CLI (for agent-side read/write) need anchor models. Following the shared/egg_contracts/ pattern, a shared package ensures consistent serialization and validation on both sides. The orchestrator imports it server-side; the sandbox CLI imports it client-side.
alternatives_considered: Orchestrator-internal module only — rejected because sandbox CLI also needs models for local file I/O
Inline in egg_contracts — rejected because anchors are conceptually distinct from pipeline contracts and have different lifecycle semantics

architecture_decisions.title: Redis-backed AnchorStore with in-memory cache
architecture_decisions.decision: Create an AnchorStore class in orchestrator/anchor_store.py following the ProgressStore pattern but with Redis persistence
architecture_decisions.rationale: Unlike progress events (ephemeral, in-memory only), anchors must survive orchestrator restarts. Redis provides persistence with minimal latency. The in-memory cache avoids Redis round-trips for frequent reads (team anchor generation). Redis key pattern: anchor:{pipeline_id}:{agent_id} following the established redis_message_store.py namespace pattern.
alternatives_considered: In-memory only like ProgressStore — rejected because orchestrator restart would lose all anchors
Git-only storage — rejected because cross-worktree reads require API mediation anyway

architecture_decisions.title: CLI subcommands via egg-orch anchor (not standalone egg-anchor CLI)
architecture_decisions.decision: Add anchor subcommands to the existing egg-orch CLI namespace
architecture_decisions.rationale: egg-orch is the established agent-facing CLI for orchestrator interactions (signal, consensus, message, progress). Anchors are orchestrator-managed state, so egg-orch anchor is the natural namespace. This avoids a new CLI entrypoint and leverages existing orchestrator URL resolution. The OrchestratorClient (shared/egg_orchestrator/client.py) handles HTTP communication.
alternatives_considered: Standalone egg-anchor CLI — rejected because anchors require orchestrator API access, making them part of the egg-orch domain

architecture_decisions.title: Pull-based recovery via standing rules (not push injection)
architecture_decisions.decision: Implement recovery via sandbox/.claude/rules/anchor-recovery.md loaded at container startup
architecture_decisions.rationale: Claude Code's compaction/clear behavior is opaque to egg — there is no compaction callback or injection hook. CLAUDE.md and rules are assembled once at startup by sandbox/entrypoint.py:setup_agent_rules(). Pull-based recovery (agent reads anchor on-demand when it detects context loss) is robust and doesn't depend on undocumented Claude Code internals. The consensus wrapper recovery prompt is also extended to include anchor loading for restart scenarios.
alternatives_considered: Push-based injection via Claude Code hooks — deferred to v2, depends on API availability
Dynamic CLAUDE.md updates — rejected because CLAUDE.md is symlinked at startup, not dynamically updated

architecture_decisions.title: Session-scoped gateway enforcement for anchor ownership
architecture_decisions.decision: Gateway validates that pushed anchor files match the agent's own agent_id using session metadata
architecture_decisions.rationale: The gateway already has session metadata (registered by container_spawner) including agent role and container ID. Anchor filename includes agent_id ({role}-{container_id}), which can be validated against session metadata. This follows the existing contract_api.py pattern where role is validated against session data, not headers or env vars. Prevents cross-agent anchor tampering without adding new auth mechanisms.
alternatives_considered: No gateway enforcement — rejected because agents could overwrite each other's anchors
Separate auth token per agent — rejected as over-engineering given session metadata already provides identity

architecture_decisions.title: Team anchor as orchestrator-generated API projection (not file)
architecture_decisions.decision: The team anchor is generated server-side by the orchestrator from individual anchors + pipeline state, served via GET /api/v1/anchors/team/{pipeline_id}
architecture_decisions.rationale: The team anchor aggregates data the orchestrator already tracks (agent statuses, heartbeats, BRC consensus state, decisions). No agent needs to write it. The coordinator role has no repository access (per CLAUDE.md), so it cannot maintain a file-based team anchor. Generating it on-demand from existing orchestrator state is simpler and always consistent.
alternatives_considered: Coordinator writes team anchor file — rejected because coordinator has no repo access
Each agent writes a team section — rejected because it creates distributed consistency problems

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Anchor staleness — agent forgets to update anchor at critical milestones
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Recovery rules in anchor-recovery.md include staleness detection (compare anchor updated_at vs current time). Agent instructions emphasize updating at natural checkpoints: sub-task completion, decisions, BRC transitions. Auto-warnings when anchor is >5 minutes stale during recovery.
risks_and_mitigations.residual_risk: Cannot force agent to update; relies on prompt compliance

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Size budget violations prevent anchor updates at critical moments
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Soft limit (2KB) warns but allows writes. Hard limit (3KB) blocks. CLI suggests pruning completed progress items and old decisions. Schema maxItems constraints (progress: 10, decisions: 8, key_context: 5) structurally prevent unbounded growth.
risks_and_mitigations.residual_risk: Agent may need to triage what to keep, potentially dropping important context

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Orchestrator restart loses in-memory anchor cache
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Redis persistence is primary store; in-memory cache is populated lazily from Redis. Git-pushed anchor files on worktree branches provide additional backup. The AnchorStore.get() method falls back to Redis on cache miss.
risks_and_mitigations.residual_risk: Brief period where cache is cold after restart; negligible impact

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Intra-agent reasoning lost on context clear — anchor preserves structure but not thought process
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Documented as known limitation in the spec. key_context field (max 5 items, 150 chars each) captures critical non-derivable context. Agents re-derive approach from code state + anchor. errors_encountered field prevents re-attempting known failures.
risks_and_mitigations.residual_risk: Agent may make different (but valid) choices post-recovery

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Concurrent anchor reads during atomic write could see partial state
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Atomic write via temp-file-then-rename (os.rename is atomic on same filesystem per POSIX). In BRC concurrent phases with shared worktrees, readers either see the old complete file or the new complete file, never a partial write.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Gateway session-scoped enforcement bypass if agent_id format changes
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Agent ID format ({role}-{short_container_id}) is generated by egg-orch anchor init from env vars (EGG_AGENT_ROLE + CONTAINER_ID). Gateway validates anchor filename against same session metadata. Both use the same generation logic in shared/egg_anchor/constants.py.
risks_and_mitigations.residual_risk: Format change requires coordinated update to both gateway and anchor init

soft_dependencies.title: Cross-agent communication
soft_dependencies.relationship: Anchors work standalone. Message bus enables last_message_id catch-up for efficient post-clear recovery. Without #1027, agents can still recover from anchor alone but miss messages sent after last anchor update.

soft_dependencies.title: Agent roster and access controls
soft_dependencies.relationship: Agent ID uses {role}-{container_id} format, decoupled from roster. Full roster integration (mapping agent IDs to display names, team membership) is v2.

no_dependency.title: Conversational coordinator
no_dependency.relationship: Team anchor is orchestrator-generated. No coordinator involvement needed.

reviewer_feedback_items.item: Add flip_flop_count + changed_artifacts to brc_state schema
reviewer_feedback_items.recommendation: Include in Phase 1 schema definition. Add flip_flop_count (integer, tracks propose/NACK cycles) and changed_artifacts (array of strings, files changed since last proposal) to brc_state object in schema.

reviewer_feedback_items.item: Define anchor seeding from predecessor on agent retry
reviewer_feedback_items.recommendation: On agent retry (new container), the orchestrator should seed the new agent's anchor from the failed agent's anchor stored in Redis. Add a --seed-from flag to egg-orch anchor init. Include in Phase 2 (orchestrator API).

reviewer_feedback_items.item: Specify _meta.sequence as tiebreaker for CLI POST vs git-push staleness
reviewer_feedback_items.recommendation: Document that _meta.sequence is a monotonically increasing counter incremented on every egg-orch anchor update call. The orchestrator only accepts updates where sequence > stored sequence. Include in Phase 1 model documentation.

reviewer_feedback_items.item: Decide anchor init location (entrypoint.py vs container_spawner)
reviewer_feedback_items.recommendation: Anchor init should happen in the sandbox entrypoint (sandbox/entrypoint.py) after setup_agent_rules(), not in container_spawner.py. This is because: (1) the sandbox has the anchor CLI available, (2) init needs to be inside the container, (3) follows the pattern of other sandbox-side setup. Container spawner only needs to pass AGENT_ANCHOR_ID env var.

reviewer_feedback_items.item: Define AC-8 proxy test — simulate compaction via agent restart
reviewer_feedback_items.recommendation: E2E test: launch agent with anchor, let it make progress, kill and restart with only anchor-recovery.md + anchor file, verify agent resumes correctly. Include in Phase 4.

q1_redis_namespace.question: Should anchors use a dedicated Redis database/prefix?
q1_redis_namespace.recommendation: Dedicated prefix anchor:{pipeline_id}:{agent_id} in the same Redis database. Consistent with pipeline:{pipeline_id}:messages pattern in redis_message_store.py. Avoids multi-database complexity.

q2_auto_pruning.question: Should CLI auto-prune old completed progress items?
q2_auto_pruning.recommendation: Warn only, agent decides. Auto-pruning risks removing context the agent considers important. The CLI should suggest pruning when approaching soft limit but not act unilaterally.

q3_non_coordinator_team_anchor.question: Should team anchor work in non-coordinator pipelines?
q3_non_coordinator_team_anchor.recommendation: Yes. The orchestrator generates team anchors from individual anchor data regardless of coordinator presence. Useful for any multi-agent phase, not just coordinator-managed ones.
